title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Eu(III) emission reports site symmetry: 5D0 is nondegenerate, so the number of Stark components of each 5D0→7FJ band reflects the degeneracy of 7FJ, and observation of 5D0→7F0 signals at least one non-centrosymmetric site with one component per such chemical environment.
explanation: 5D0→7F0 is formally forbidden; its appearance is attributed to J-mixing (and/or charge-transfer mixing) in Cn, Cnv, or Cs symmetries, where 7F0 borrows J = 2, 4, 6 character. Relative intensity of hypersensitive 5D0→7F2 further tracks local asymmetry, coordination number, and ligand polarizability.
scope: Eu(III) in complexes, glasses, and crystalline hosts used as a spectroscopic probe, including CPL design.
conditions: Maximum splitting is 2J+1 for non-Kramers Eu(III); at most three 5D0→7F1 components per non-equivalent site.
caveats: Absence of 5D0→7F0 does not by itself prove inversion symmetry if the line is simply too weak to detect.
